For the briefest moment in the early 2000s, Butt Rock ruled the airwaves. Creed wanted to take you higher. Nickelback were asking if we were having fun yet. And the guy from a band called Hoobastank wanted you to know he was not a perfect person. It was music that provided the perfect slightly angsty soundtrack for your morning commute, and one of the last fleeting glimpses of rock music as a chart entity. 

All were using elements of Grunge, the gruff baritone, garbled sincerity and quiet loud dynamics, but buffed and polished with a view to radio and arena-glory, uninterested in the anti-sellout punk ethics of the original Seattle bands. But how did Butt Rock happen? What were their influences, the vital steps along the way? And how did we get to the point where the credibility completely disappeared from grunge? These are the 7 Songs to Blame For Butt Rock.

#postgrunge #
title: The 7 Songs To Blame For Butt Rock
